candidate.title: Break-seq
candidate.scope: The Break-seq row of the supplied Illumina schematic: agarose-embedded broken chromosomal DNA is biotin end-labeled, released and fragmented, affinity captured, adaptor equipped, and amplified/purified into a DNA sequencing library. This is the Break-seq implementation associated with Hoffman et al., Genome Research 25:402–412 (2015), PMID 25609572, DOI 10.1101/gr.180497.114. The supplied crop also shows separate PB-seq, Pu-seq and LAM-HTGTS rows; the assigned card targets Break-seq alone. Replication-fork breakage is the illustrated biological context. The final material is DNA enriched around label-accessible break ends; sequencing and genomic mapping are an interpretive readout supported by the paper, beyond the drawn library endpoint. The capture selects labeled DNA and permits background signal; it does not establish complete or perfectly specific recovery of biological breaks.

operations.label: Elution and fragmentation
operations.description: Release the labeled chromosomal DNA from agarose and fragment it into shorter duplex molecules, retaining a subset carrying the prior biotin label. The diagram groups release and fragmentation in one block. For the matched implementation, the primary paper identifies electroelution as the Break-seq release procedure; the catalogue prose instead describes agarase digestion (see correction c_release).
operations.mechanism: Electroelution is supported by the primary paper’s explicit comparison with Break-chip. Shearing follows DNA-end labeling in the primary Break-seq description.
operations.information_effect: Preserves the prior biotin label on a subset of fragments while creating additional fragment ends after labeling.

corrections.diagram_observation: The Break-seq row says Elution and fragmentation without specifying a release reagent. The verified secondary catalogue narrative says the agarose is digested by b-agarase. The drawn block and its outgoing route are retained.
corrections.primary_statement: The primary paper’s Methods: Break-chip paragraph explicitly says that β-agarase digestion replaces the electroelution described for Break-seq. The matched Break-seq implementation is therefore interpreted as using electroelution within the depicted release/fragmentation block. The catalogue’s agarase wording is not imported into the Break-seq graph, and Break-chip is not added as another target method.

unknowns.question: Does adaptor attachment occur while the DNA remains bead-bound, and when is it released for amplification? The schematic changes from a bead-bound icon to an adaptor-bearing duplex without naming a release, and the inspected main paper gives only the capture-to-library sequence. A primary detailed library-construction description would resolve this attachment-state transition; no extra release operation is asserted. The inspected main-text Break-seq methods section [b00059] delegates detailed library construction to Supplemental Material.

checks.rationale: The correction distinguishes the nonspecific drawn Elution and fragmentation block from the secondary catalogue’s agarase claim. The primary paper explicitly contrasts β-agarase extraction in Break-chip with electroelution in Break-seq. Applying electroelution only to the matched Break-seq release block preserves the drawn route and does not introduce Break-chip as a target.
